title: Crüger to Müller, Easter Monday 1631
author: Peter Crüger
source: Peter Crüger's letter to Philipp Müller of Easter Monday 1631, written at Danzig after the news of Kepler's death had reached him. Müller quoted its second passage in his letter to Jacob Bartsch of 8 May 1631. The original is in the Bibliothèque de l'Observatoire, Paris (B, 1, 9; 89, 9. R. 39). Printed in extracts in *Nova Kepleriana* 4, ed. Walther von Dyck and Max Caspar, Abhandlungen der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften, Math.-naturw. Abteilung 31, no. 1 (Munich, 1927), 110.
transcribed_from: the page images of the 1927 printing.
summary: Crüger mourns Kepler, regretting the unfinished works he had promised, and declines to write a funeral poem.

notes.note: Kepler's planned *Hipparchus*, on the sizes and distances of the sun, moon and earth, never finished.
After Plautus, *Asinaria* 202: “our hands always have eyes; they believe what they see.”
